statement: Starting from an exact clean approved baseline descended from 82b54ef9b7c8d6be9f2d6450cbc5e6713ade00af, the raft-rs partition snapshot owner creates, transfers, installs and restarts a real file-backed application image for an intact durable lagging member without losing schema, indexes, acknowledged rows or committed transaction state at or below the included applied boundary, and later committed entries remain replayable. The payload excludes source-local HardState, vote, lifecycle incarnation and runtime tables. The receiver preserves its exact local identity/incarnation and election-safe term/vote. Publication epoch and durable group membership generation remain independent owner facts. Recovery class is derived from its named owners, never caller mode. Opening an existing replica validates local durable reconstruction prerequisites through their existing owners: exact identity and peer reservations, active lifecycle/incarnation, canonical and internally coherent HardState term/vote, and durable log/snapshot/applied/configuration facts. Missing, unreadable, corrupt or internally contradictory local prerequisites refuse unsafe core reconstruction and participation; valid vote=0 and a coherent locally lagging configuration are not defects. Known destructive absence with authoritative prior existence produces the existing local reseed HOLD. Opening an intact durable replica does not require newly obtained live-majority membership proof. The sender publishes a private Storage-owned native snapshot only after sealing and fsyncing the application image plus proof manifest, atomically recording the published binding and permitted compaction boundary in the existing durable store, and then compacting native storage from that durable record. MemStorage::apply_snapshot is receiver restore only and is never used to publish a live sender snapshot. The sender may publish a validated historical boundary B with exact term/history and ConfState/generation at B, retains and replays every committed entry after B, and does not require current-applied equality that would starve under continuous writes. An intact receiver accepts an application snapshot only as the state-machine image bound to an exact snapshot accepted by its own live raft-rs runtime and emitted in that runtime's Ready. The receiver's Raft term/index/configuration rules decide consensus admissibility; exact group, target identity and service generation, snapshot index/term, ConfState/configuration generation, application boundary, native snapshot metadata/data and payload digest bind that decision to the installed image. This is not a claim that the sender retains present majority connectivity or that the snapshot contains the latest configuration at wall-clock install time. A historically committed delayed prefix may be accepted when the receiver's Raft rules admit it, and later committed entries replay in order. An unaccepted, mismatched, superseded or invalid image binding cannot install. After receiver Ready acceptance, the host atomically commits the exact application image together with Ready durability and applied/configuration state in the same main SQLite database before snapshot acknowledgement, application exposure or advance. No durable half-applied Ready state is permitted. Crash/restart observes either the old coherent state or the new coherent state; lost response resolves from the exact durable completion binding. Active or LOCAL_STAGING transactions drain or terminate through their own owner, never arbitrary rollback or timeout shortening. The same live service may continue after owner-controlled cache/session reconstruction, and a successor service generation fences stale work. This Quest does not claim a separate accepted-image debt marker or service re-registration requirement. Pre-acceptance refusal leaves the prior intact service safe and registered. Local identity/incarnation/reservations and receiver-owned election state remain authoritative; source election state is never imported. No fresh majority proof is required for ordinary intact local reconstruction or as an additional snapshot policy. Fresh CREATE and known-wipe HOLD remain separate existing-owner decisions. A fresh learner component install requires exact CREATE admission, physical-worker claim and committed learner reservation. A detected wiped replica is never reconstructed as the same voter; exact retirement and fresh-identity learner replacement remain a separately sealed parked membership obligation. Manual restoration or rollback of a previous whole replica DB image is unsupported and outside this Quest. Production registered dispatch, real bulk receive, intact install/restart and refusal use one owner interaction, with no legacy fallback, caller-selected recovery mode, source-election-state copy or second persistence, consensus, membership, lifecycle or cleanup owner. Manual invocation of the registered callback proves only the bounded interaction; automatic lag detection/cadence and wiped-member fresh-identity rebuild remain full-cutover obligations. This Quest neither resurrects a wiped same voter nor unparks FreshMG.

constraints.statement: The Quest keeps LOCAL_OPEN, KNOWN_WIPE, INSTALL_ADMISSION and READ_UNAVAILABLE separate. LOCAL_OPEN reconstructs only from exact target-local durable facts. KNOWN_WIPE is only readable current storage with absent durable Raft record plus authoritative prior existence. INSTALL_ADMISSION requires a receiver-native accepted snapshot Ready and exact application-image binding. READ_UNAVAILABLE blocks only the transition whose fact owner is unavailable and never fabricates absence, HOLD or install permission.

Opening an intact durable replica requires exact identity and peer reservations, active lifecycle/incarnation, canonical and internally coherent HardState term/vote and durable log/snapshot/applied/ConfState/generation facts. Vote 0 and coherent local lag are valid. Three intact voters must be able to cold restart without a preexisting live leader, elect and commit an ordinary entry.

When the exact current DB is readable but lacks the durable Raft record and the authoritative prior-existence owner proves the identity opened before, the production owner refuses reseed-required before native core entry and persists a current-DB lifecycle HOLD. Same-byte restart repeats the refusal. This Quest makes no safe-refusal or no-effect claim for manual old-image rollback or restore of a previous whole replica DB.

An intact-member install is authorized only by a snapshot accepted by the receiver's actual live raft-rs core and emitted in Ready, bound to the exact application image by group, target identity, service generation, snapshot index/term, ConfState/configuration generation, application boundary, native snapshot metadata/data and payload digest. Bulk transfer may validate and stage immutable bytes and return AWAITING_NATIVE_SNAPSHOT, but staging alone is not consensus rejection and not install authority. Native data/Ready/staged descriptor/image/lifecycle mismatch refuses before application import with native_snapshot_binding_mismatch; an actual native packet that produces no accepted snapshot Ready is native_snapshot_not_admitted for image installation only. Descriptors, source assertions, cache rows, publication freshness, caller flags, injected Ready and mocked runtime answers do not authorize install. The application image is imported atomically with Ready durability and applied/configuration state in the same main database before acknowledgement, exposure or advance.

Sender publication uses private Storage under the existing native wrapper: ordinary initial_state/entries/term/first_index/last_index remain delegated through an explicit compacted-boundary overlay, snapshot(request_index,to) returns only the exact published sealed Snapshot or SnapshotTemporarilyUnavailable, and publication is durable-first. Before v2 capture, the source obtains stable cluster identity through the existing authoritative CONFIG owner-RPC path; cache hydration miss, default cluster id, local SQL fallback, unreadable identity or established mismatch yields a typed checkpoint creation refusal before capture/publication/compaction. The owner seals/fsyncs bytes, atomically persists published binding and permitted compaction boundary, then installs the exact published snapshot in private native storage and compacts. MemStorage::apply_snapshot is receiver restore only and is never used to publish on a live sender. Native-first then SQLite failure is forbidden; retry reads the exact durable publication idempotently. Private report_snapshot feedback and bounded retry are owned by the runtime around genuine emitted MsgSnapshot attempts, not by caller flags or fabricated delivery success.

A valid sender snapshot may use a historical boundary B from one consistent copied state with B at or below durable applied, exact term/history checks, matching full ConfState/generation at B and monotonic immutable publication. The sender retains and replays every committed entry after B, including later configuration changes. Publication does not require B/config/generation to equal current applied facts at send time, because that would starve under continuous writes.

A registered file-backed source image contains application schema, indexes, acknowledged rows and committed transaction state through its applied boundary, refuses an undecided prepared state before publication unless separately proved by its owner, and excludes source HardState, vote, lifecycle incarnation and runtime tables. LOCAL_STAGING sessions must drain or terminate through their own owner before an image is published or installed.

Publication epoch and durable group membershipGenerationIndex remain independent owner facts. Publication freshness fences routing only. Durable group generation binds ConfState provenance, application boundary and native snapshot manifest/data, while sender-local applied/HardState/log/lifecycle tables remain excluded from the payload. A v2 application image contains exactly one raft_rs_checkpoint_manifest(singleton, manifest_json) table whose canonical manifest M has payloadVersion 2 and no membershipEpoch. Descriptor D carries membershipEpoch 9 as the routing/publication freshness fact while M and D carry group generation 0; native data N is canonical {bindingVersion:1, checkpoint:C} with membershipEpoch omitted from C. Canonical wrong generation is proved by mutating only D.raftRs.membershipGenerationIndex while payload bytes/M/native data remain unchanged: structural descriptor validation stays VALID, readCheckpoint returns CORRUPT_PAYLOAD with RAFT_RS_CHECKPOINT_REASON.MANIFEST_GENERATION_MISMATCH, and malformed decimal syntax remains a separate descriptor control.

The receiver preserves target-owned identity, lifecycle/incarnation and election state. Term never regresses; same-term vote is preserved; legitimate higher-term vote reset is receiver-owned; source election state is never imported. Refusal or invalid binding preserves application/lifecycle/install artifacts while allowing only receiver-native consensus writes that the actual core performs.

Fresh learner component installation remains a separate component path requiring exact ReplicaCreateAdmissionOwner evidence, physical-worker claim, operation/admission/attempt identity, current learner reservation and exact generation. R5 requires REPLACE source retention when source_replica_id is present, genuine branded A/B evidence and physical-worker claims at the install boundary, duplicate retry, terminal-first/admission-first, release/reclaim rotation, wrong role/worker/identity/successor-generation refusals, and explicit late-CREATE/admission fencing: a stale A CREATE claim after A closure and B admission is refused while B bytes/artifacts remain preserved. Exact-generation cleanup protects successor bytes and artifacts; cleanup uncertainty preserves the replica without turning cleanup into operation settlement debt. Existing payloadVersion 1 fresh-CREATE artifacts remain version-dispatched under CREATE/worker/learner authority and are never an intact-install fallback; any v2 fresh-CREATE use must prove the same authority plus app import or return typed unsupported. It does not unpark FreshMG or authorize wiped-voter resurrection.

Pre-acceptance refusal preserves the prior intact service. After receiver Ready acceptance, the host atomically commits Ready durability, application import, applied/configuration state and exact completion binding in the same main SQLite database before acknowledgement, exposure or advance. Crash/restart observes old coherent state or new coherent state; lost response resolves from exact completion binding. The same service may continue after owner-controlled cache/session reconstruction; successor generation fences stale work. A pending image stage or cleanup uncertainty never grants operation settlement, membership cleanup, deletion, member-lane release or install authority. Legitimate terminal operation settlement proceeds under its own operation owner and must not be indefinitely blocked by snapshot staging or cleanup uncertainty. Unaccepted staging has bounded transfer-owned retention and may expire with exact pin/marker cleanup; that expiration neither settles an operation nor deletes a replica or successor artifact. No separate durable accepted-image debt marker or re-registration claim is made. Operation settlement, membership, cleanup and deletion remain separate authorities.

The test-receipt probe reads receipt IDs, booleans, receipt statuses and overall status from the receipt file produced by scripts/quest-evidence/harness-runtime.js. Acting harnesses run outside probe mode, refuse under LAGRANGE_PROBE=1 and use harness-runtime as the existing binary runner. The abandoned custom digest/result generator is not an authority and must not be used for Path B. Baseline red runs may and normally do write failing runner receipts; the probe and external review must measure those exact fail receipts rather than relying on hand-written summaries. Exact command/environment, source HEAD, relevant dirty source/test/runner hashes, complete output/exit, raw-log digest, owner-entry evidence and reached/unreached classification are external manifest and independent-review obligations, not claims made by a generator or the probe. A current red supports sealing only when it reaches the relevant production owner and fails at the intended missing transition; setup/import/fixture failures, skip/todo/zero-selected cases, hand-set pass flags and reused downstream diagnostics are unmeasured. All seven concrete future-green suites must exist and be independently reviewed before Quest seal, even if some baseline runs are red or blocked by earlier owner transitions.

This draft is unsealed planning only. It does not authorize source, alter or supersede the active higher Quest itself, edit the epic, start this Quest, promote partial diagnostics to receipts, or unpark FreshMG. Before sealing/source, independent review must approve exact owner interaction and scope, seven concrete future-green suites and acting harness, external exact-baseline manifests, runner-produced baseline receipts for genuine reds where available, and at least one genuine baseline owner red while rejecting setup-only or skipped failures. No R7 absence or BLOCKED placeholder can satisfy the seven-suite preseal requirement. After sealing/source, exact-candidate all-required greens, semantic revert/crash mutants and independent verification are required before landing.

New v2 source image authoring requires a stable durable cluster identity from the existing authoritative CONFIG owner-RPC path before capture. SeedRegistrationPhase remains the identity creation workflow. Snapshot code may consume the typed authoritative singleton and compare it to admitted local cluster/group/entity facts, but may not mint identity, use cache/default/SQL fallback, or gate receiver install/opening of already native-admitted images on a recurring CONFIG majority lease.

Real native MsgSnapshot attempts are observed from Ready.messages and retain the unchanged native packet while bulk staging completes. The existing private runtime facade owns report_snapshot(handle, peer, finish|failure), stale-attempt rejection, bounded retry/reconcile demand and RawNode::ping liveness nudges. Transport completion, failure or loss cannot fabricate native admission, advance match/next, or manufacture a Ready; native responses and later Ready own progress.

R4 final evidence must use the supported local-open/known-wipe/cold-restart owner scope. It must exercise pre-create_node refusals or typed owner failures for missing, unreadable, corrupt or contradictory HardState, log, snapshot, applied, ConfState, generation, lifecycle, identity, reservation and group facts; prove no unsafe install, campaign, vote or same-identity participation per fact; preserve legal vote=0 and coherent lag positives; keep read-unavailable distinct from absence/HOLD; and pair with same-byte known-wipe HOLD replay plus three-voter cold restart. Historical old-clone rollback diagnostics remain excluded from the final supported-fault receipt.
